title: Localized simplicial Grothendieck construction computes a poset homotopy colimit
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, their model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ and derived localization $L_WC$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Fix containing universes. Let $A$ be a small partially ordered set and $p:A\to\mathrm{sCat}$ a strict diagram. For $a\leq b$ write $p_{ab}:p(a)\to p(b)$ for its transition functor. Define a simplicial category $E(p)$ with objects $(a,x)$ for $x\in p(a)$ and the following mapping simplicial sets: if $a\leq b$, put
$$E(p)((a,x),(b,y))=p(b)(p_{ab}x,y);$$
if $a\nleq b$, this mapping simplicial set is empty.
Composition applies $p_{bc}$ to the first arrow and then composes in $p(c)$; identities are the fiber identities. Let $W(p)$ consist of the vertex arrows $(a,x)\to(b,p_{ab}x)$ represented by $1_{p_{ab}x}$, for all $a\leq b$. Suppose the ordinary diagram category $\mathrm{sCat}^{A}$ has the projective model structure, whose weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise. For a projectively cofibrant replacement $Qp\to p$, put $\operatorname{hocolim}_A p=\operatorname{colim}_A Qp$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$L_{W(p)}E(p)\cong\operatorname{hocolim}_A p\quad\text{in }h\mathrm{sCat}.$$
For every strict cocone $p\to\operatorname{const}T$, the induced functor $E(p)\to T$ sends $W(p)$ to identities. Under the displayed isomorphism its derived localization map agrees with the comparison $\operatorname{hocolim}_A p\to T$ induced by this cocone. The isomorphism is natural for transformations of diagrams and cocones and includes $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.11, Lemmas A.3.5.12--A.3.5.13, with Proposition A.3.5.10, printed pp.894--896 (PDF pp.912--914). The natural cocone clause follows the actual maps π_a in A.3.5.11--12 and the projective replacement in A.3.5.10. Read independently 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-category result.

proof.text: Write $E=E(p)$ and $W=W(p)$. The composition in the statement is associative because $p_{bc}p_{ab}=p_{ac}$ strictly and every transition preserves composition; the fiber identity vertices are units. The grade $d(a,x)=a$ has $E(u,v)=\varnothing$ unless $d(u)\leq d(v)$. Use the fixed $[1]\to K\to\mathbb J$ and strict localization $\Gamma$ of the arrow-attachment node. Its comparison identifies $\Gamma(E,W)$ with $L_WE$ under $E$, including the maps induced by functors sending $W$ to identities. For each $a$ let $E_a=E_{\leq a}$ and $W_a$ be the labels in $W$ with both endpoints in $E_a$. Inclusions define the strict diagram $\chi(a)=\Gamma(E_a,W_a)$ and its strict cocone $\ell_a:\chi(a)\to\Gamma(E,W)$.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.11, Remark A.3.5.8 and Notation A.3.5.1; choice of the strict localization model is supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: Define $r_a:E_a\to p(a)$ by $r_a(b,x)=p_{ba}x$. On a mapping simplex $u\in p(c)(p_{bc}x,y)$, for $b\leq c\leq a$, set $r_a(u)=p_{ca}(u)$. Its source is $p_{ca}p_{bc}x=p_{ba}x$, so it is a simplicial functor and sends every label of $W_a$ to an identity. Let $C_a$ be the full subcategory on $b<a$, and put $f_a=r_a|_{C_a}$. The remaining objects of $E_a$ form precisely $p(a)$. Mapping sets inside either part are unchanged, the mapping set from $(b,x)$ with $b<a$ to $(a,y)$ is $p(a)(p_{ba}x,y)$, and every mapping set in the reverse direction is empty. These identifications respect composition by the displayed formula for $r_a$. Thus $E_a$ is exactly the categorical mapping cylinder $M_{f_a}$ and $r_a$ is its canonical retraction.

source.place: Definition A.3.5.11 and the identification used in Lemma A.3.5.12 with Lemma A.3.5.6; all mapping sets and compositions are computed here.

proof.text: For each $(b,x)$ with $b<a$, the required cross arrow $(b,x)\to(a,p_{ba}x)$ lies in $W_a$, and $r_a$ sends every label of $W_a$, including transitions between lower fibers, to an identity. The mapping-cylinder node therefore says that the specified extension $\rho_a:\chi(a)\to p(a)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. For $a\leq a'$, the equations $p_{aa'}r_a=r_{a'}|_{E_a}$ hold on objects and every mapping simplex, since $p_{aa'}p_{ca}=p_{ca'}$. Both extensions collapse each attached $K$ through its specified map to $\mathbb J$ and then to the common object. They therefore agree on those copies too. Consequently $\rho:\chi\to p$ is a strict objectwise weak equivalence of diagrams.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.12 and the natural transformation of diagrams at the end of Definition A.3.5.11.

proof.text: Apply the filtered-resolution node to $E$ with its grade $d$. Obtain $f:E'\to E$ bijective on objects, locally a trivial Kan fibration, with $D'(a)=E'_{\leq a}$ projectively cofibrant as an $A$-diagram. Identify its object set with that of $E$. For each labelled $w\in W$ choose a vertex lift $w'$ between the corresponding objects: trivial Kan fibrations lift $\partial\Delta^0\to\Delta^0$ by the Kan-model node. Keep the original label set $W$ for these chosen arrows. If the target of $w$ has grade $b$, then its source has grade at most $b$, and $w'$ lies in $E'_{\leq a}$ precisely for $b\leq a$. Put $\chi'(a)=\Gamma(E'_{\leq a},W_a)$ using these lifts. Each restriction of $f$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, so arrow-attachment invariance gives an objectwise weak equivalence $\chi'\to\chi$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.9 and the first sentence of the proof of Proposition A.3.5.10, with the explicit vertex-lifting argument.

proof.text: The diagram $\chi'$ is projectively cofibrant, as can be checked directly by lifting. For a diagram $X\to Y$ which is objectwise a trivial fibration and a map $\chi'\to Y$, first lift its restriction $D'\to Y$ to $X$, using projective cofibrancy of $D'$. For a label $w$ whose target has grade $b$, its attaching $[1]$ and its copy of $K$ first occur at $b$ and occur at every $a\geq b$. At $b$ the chosen lift on $D'(b)$ and the given map $K\to Y(b)$ form a lifting square for the cofibration $i:[1]\to K$ against $X(b)\to Y(b)$. Choose a lift $K\to X(b)$ and propagate it to every $X(a)$ for $a\geq b$. Diagram functoriality makes these propagated maps compatible. Do this independently for every label. The pushout universal property now gives compatible maps $\chi'(a)\to X(a)$ lifting the given diagram map. This is the left lifting property defining projective cofibrancy; no objectwise-cofibrancy-to-projective-cofibrancy implication is used.

source.place: Expanded projective-cofibrancy assertion in the proof of Proposition A.3.5.10; explicit principal-upper-set attachment lifting.

proof.text: There are canonical ordinary colimit identifications $\operatorname{colim}_a E'_{\leq a}=E'$ and $\operatorname{colim}_a\chi'(a)=\Gamma(E',W)$. Indeed compatible enriched functors from the initial segments glue uniquely: an object of grade $b$ occurs already at $b$, each mapping simplex from grade $b$ to grade $c$ occurs at $c$, and every composable string occurs at the grade of its last target. Thus all identities and composition equations are checked in one initial segment. For the second identification, use the pushout description: for a label with target grade $b$, a compatible family of maps on its copies of $K$ is exactly one map on the copy at $b$, because the indexing upper set has initial element $b$. Hence compatible functors $\chi'(a)\to T$ are exactly a functor $E'\to T$ and one map $K\to T$ per label, agreeing on $[1]$. This is precisely the defining pushout property of $\Gamma(E',W)$. The same argument without primes identifies $\operatorname{colim}\chi=\Gamma(E,W)$ and identifies its colimit cocone with $\ell$.

source.place: Remark A.3.5.8 and the colimit identifications in the proof of Proposition A.3.5.10; universal-property verification written out.

proof.text:
The map $\operatorname{colim}\chi'\to\operatorname{colim}\chi$ is, under Step 6, exactly $\Gamma(E',W)\to\Gamma(E,W)$ induced by $f$. It is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by arrow-attachment invariance. The adjunction $\operatorname{colim}_A\dashv\operatorname{const}_A$ is Quillen for the assumed projective model structure: its right adjoint preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations since these are objectwise. Apply the derived-functor assertion of the Quillen node. Steps 4--5 give a projectively cofibrant diagram weakly equivalent to $\chi$, so its colimit computes $\mathbf L\operatorname{colim}(\chi)$. The preceding weak equivalence therefore says that the comparison induced by the actual cocone $\ell$ is an isomorphism
$$\kappa:\operatorname{hocolim}_A\chi\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma(E,W)\quad\text{in }h\mathrm{sCat}.$$
The map $\chi'\to\chi$ need not be a trivial fibration; a weak equivalence with cofibrant source suffices for computing the derived functor.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.3.5.10, expanded using its stated cofibrant resolution and localization invariance; ordinary Quillen derived-colimit comparison.

proof.text: Since $\rho:\chi\to p$ is an objectwise weak equivalence in the projective model structure, it is an isomorphism in that model homotopy category. The derived functor $\mathbf L\operatorname{colim}_A$ of the Quillen node sends it to an isomorphism $v:\operatorname{hocolim}_A\chi\to\operatorname{hocolim}_A p$. Define the desired comparison by $\theta=v\kappa^{-1}$, after identifying $\Gamma(E,W)$ with $L_WE$ by the arrow-attachment node. This proves the displayed isomorphism. It is defined using $\rho$ and the actual cocone $\ell$, rather than by assigning the same isomorphism class to two objects.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.13, obtained from Lemma A.3.5.12 and Proposition A.3.5.10; maps of the cocones retained.

proof.text:
Let $c_a:p(a)\to T$ be a strict cocone. Define $G:E\to T$ by $G(a,x)=c_a(x)$ and, for $u\in p(b)(p_{ab}x,y)$, by $G(u)=c_b(u)$, with source $c_b p_{ab}x=c_a x$. Strict cocone compatibility and the composition formula for $E$ make this an enriched functor, and $G$ sends every label of $W$ to an identity. Let $\bar G:\Gamma(E,W)\to T$ be its specified identity-collapse extension. On $E_a$ one has $G|_{E_a}=c_a r_a$, and on each attached $K$ both extensions use the same identity collapse. Thus there is an equality of strict cocones $\bar G\ell_a=c_a\rho_a$. Applying the derived colimit functor and its natural comparison to ordinary cocone maps gives
$$\bar G\kappa=(\operatorname{hocolim}_A p\longrightarrow T)\,v.$$
Here the right comparison is computed by $Qp\to p\xrightarrow{c}\operatorname{const}T$ followed by ordinary colimit. Composing with $\kappa^{-1}$ proves $\bar G=(\operatorname{hocolim}_A p\to T)\theta$, exactly the requested agreement of maps.

source.place: Identity-collapse extensions in Notation A.3.5.1, the maps in Definition A.3.5.11, and the actual colimit comparison in Proposition A.3.5.10; cocone equality checked explicitly.

proof.text: For a strict transformation $\eta:p\to\widetilde p$, the induced enriched functor sends $(a,x)$ to $(a,\eta_a x)$ and a mapping simplex $u$ over $a\leq b$ to $\eta_b(u)$. Strict naturality gives $\eta_b p_{ab}=\widetilde p_{ab}\eta_a$, so it preserves the labels, initial segments, and the retractions $r_a$. Functoriality of $\Gamma$ and of the identity-collapse extensions therefore makes the maps $\rho$ and cocones $\ell$ natural. The derived functor and its comparison are natural, and inverses of natural isomorphisms are natural, so $\theta=v\kappa^{-1}$ commutes with transformations of diagrams. The equality in Step 9 then also commutes with maps of strict cocones, including a change of target $T$. Choices in the auxiliary resolution of Step 4 do not enter this definition of $\theta$.

source.place: Functorial maps in Definition A.3.5.11 and the comparison in Lemma A.3.5.13; naturality verified from the explicit maps.

proof.text: If $A=\varnothing$, then $E$ and $W$ are empty and the ordinary pushout $\Gamma(E,W)$ is the empty simplicial category. The empty diagram is already projectively cofibrant, and its colimit is the same initial simplicial category. There is exactly one strict cocone to any $T$ and exactly one functor from that initial object to $T$. Thus both the isomorphism and all compatibility claims hold in this case. The arguments above impose no nonemptiness conditions on individual fibers either.

source.place: Empty-index case of Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.8 and Lemma A.3.5.13, checked directly.
